_comment: Capstone activation-allocation finding (2026-07-03 DECISION_LEDGER), env-gated SWEG_PERSISTENT_NOMINATION, default OFF. This is an ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE PILOTING HEURISTIC, NOT a Warhammer 40,000 10th-edition game rule — there is no codex or core rule that forces an army to keep pointing its anti-tank at one enemy model across rounds; sustained focus fire is a player-level tactic. Following the precedent of simulator.focus_fire, simulator.target_economics and simulator.focus_fire_completion (all explicitly-flagged AI design heuristics), this entry quotes the core Shooting-sequence target-selection wording the heuristic operates within, and cites the real-world anti-brick doctrine that motivates it: commit anti-tank to ONE durable enemy chassis and finish it across successive rounds rather than re-spreading fire each turn. THE FINDING this reshape answers (capstone waterfall instrument, N=12+12 paired): of ~77 theoretical anti-Knight expected wounds per game only 11.4 percent is ever pointed at a Knight; conversion is clean (realized/theoretical 1.34x) — the gap is ALLOCATION. The wave-101 collective focus-fire nominator (simulator.focus_fire) exists but gates on cracking ~0.85 of a 26-wound brick's wounds in a SINGLE Shooting phase (~22 expected wounds), a bar the field almost never clears, so it never nominates and fire falls through to the lowest-health min-picker (which prefers killable War Dogs over the durable chassis). This heuristic replaces that one-phase bar with a cross-round commitment and holds the nomination until the brick dies. The mechanic does not change combat math or draw any new random number — it only re-points the existing shooting pickers' choice among already-legal in-range, in-line-of-sight candidates.

simulator.persistent_nomination.rule_name: Select Targets (10e Core Rules, Shooting phase) — persistent cross-round anti-brick focus-fire piloting heuristic
simulator.persistent_nomination.quoted_text: Each time a unit is selected to shoot, you must first select the target unit(s) for all the ranged weapons its models are equipped with, before any of those attacks are resolved.
simulator.persistent_nomination.trigger: SWEG_PERSISTENT_NOMINATION=1 (default off, byte-identical when unset). Once per army per Shooting phase (Battle._nominate_focusfire_target delegates to Battle._nominate_persistent_target before the wave-101 one-phase path runs). RE-AFFIRM: if the army already holds a standing nominee (army._persistent_nom_uid) that is still alive, still a durable brick (MONSTER / VEHICLE / TITANIC or a model with 8+ wounds), and still woundable by at least one alive friendly shooter (simulator._ranged_expected_wounds > 0), the same nominee is re-published on the _focusfire_target_uid channel both shooting pickers consume, and it is NOT reset between rounds. RE-NOMINATE: otherwise (no nominee, or the nominee died, is no longer a brick, or the army can no longer wound it) select the highest-threat brick whose summed one-round expected wounds from every unit that can wound it can bring it down within Battle._PERSISTENT_CRACK_ROUNDS (three) rounds of sustained fire — a genuinely uncrackable brick, or an army carrying only small arms that each contribute zero expected wounds against the brick, is never nominated and no fire is redirected.
simulator.persistent_nomination.effect: AI shooting target-selection heuristic. Reshapes the wave-101 collective focus-fire nomination (simulator.focus_fire) from a one-phase crack test — which demands the army crack ~0.85 of a durable brick's wounds in a single Shooting phase (~22 expected wounds against a 26-wound Knight), a bar durable bricks almost never clear, so the nominator effectively never fires — into a persistent multi-round commitment that nominates a brick crackable within a handful of rounds and holds that nomination across rounds until the brick dies, then re-nominates the next brick. Anti-tank-capable weapons prefer the standing nominee strongly: the squad split-fire planner (Battle._plan_squad_fire, default-on) concentrates only _is_antiarmour_weapon models on it, so small arms keep their normal lowest-effective-health economy (chaff clearing) and the commitment is CLASS-shaped, never army-wide — the batch lesson from the per-faction target-selection levers (Votann on-objective, Chaos Knights below-half helped; the rejected T'au single-Spotted-target bias over-concentrated and dragged the metric via closed-matrix collateral). The contest-pool filter in Battle._do_shoot (pool = contesting or candidates), which would otherwise drop an off-objective brick from the target pool and silently un-point the commitment, re-admits the nominee under this same gate when the acting model can actually reach it. This is an AI design heuristic, not a 10e rule — the quoted core target-selection wording (the whole unit's targets are chosen before any attack resolves) is the decision point the heuristic acts on; it does not alter any dice, roll, or damage value, it only changes which already-legal target the AI's shooting pickers select. Faithful and even-handed: it fires for ALL factions against ANY durable enemy brick, it does not fabricate damage (an uncrackable brick is never nominated, so no fire is wasted), and it composes with the existing screen / synapse / transport / oath / class-bias / target-economics / focus-fire-completion chain rather than replacing any combat math.

_target_priority_doctrine_reference: Real-play doctrine motivating this heuristic, presented as doctrine (not a rules citation) per the same disclosure pattern as the _target_priority_doctrine_reference notes in data/rule_citations.d/target_economics.json and data/rule_citations.d/focus_fire_completion.json: competitive anti-Knight play commits anti-tank to ONE chosen Knight and finishes that chassis across successive rounds ('focus one chassis to death per turn') rather than re-spreading fire each turn, because removing a Knight is a matter of crossing its wound threshold over the game, not of cracking it in any one phase. Sources: https://www.goonhammer.com/start-competing-imperial-knights/ (Goonhammer's Imperial Knights faction-focus guide, already cited by simulator.focus_fire, simulator.target_economics and simulator.focus_fire_completion in this project for the same 'commit fire where it can register' doctrine) and https://www.tabletopbattles.com/10th-edition-competitive-faction-focus-chaos-knights/ (already cited in data/overrides.json's DESPOILER-GUN-BUILD note and by simulator.focus_fire_completion for this project's Chaos Knights matchup sourcing). NOTE (honesty about verification): consistent with the note recorded for simulator.focus_fire_completion in this codebase, WebFetch on both URLs returned no retrievable page text in prior sessions (the pages are JavaScript-rendered), so the exact phrasing above could not be re-confirmed against live text; both domains are nonetheless real, already-vetted Knights-matchup sources elsewhere in this repository, and the 'absolute focus-fire on one Knight' doctrine paraphrased here is the same one docs/PILOT_FINDINGS.md already recorded (workflow anti-knight-research, sourced Goonhammer / Wahapedia / tabletopbattles) as the shared real-playbook tactic across the Astra Militarum, Chaos Knights and Leagues of Votann matchups versus Imperial Knights, and the same one the 2026-07-03 capstone waterfall instrument quantified as the missing allocation mechanism.
